newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end up firmer, Florida weather eyed.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end up firmer, Florida weather eyed.

text.p: FCOJ futures ended firmer as the market continued to claw its way back up following Wednesday's plunge to a four-year low, traders said.
A broker noted some trade scale down buying and the chart outlook pointed to a further advance on the upside.
"I am looking for the market to rally to 84.00 cents in the March contract and in May to 87.00 cents," the broker said. But once those levels were achieved, the market may well go down.
March frozen concentrated orange juice settled 1.60 cents firmer at 78.50 cents per pound, traded 79.50 to 76.80 cents. May went out 1.30 cents higher at 81.35 cents.
Traders said they were also keeping an eye on next week's weather in Florida's citrus belt when cooler weather was expected in the region.
David Taylor of Weather Services Corp said a cold front entered north Florida Friday afternoon and was pushing south with temperatures reaching about 40 degrees Fahrenheit Sunday morning.
There was a chance of cooler weather in the belt Tuesday evening and into Wednesday. "But we really don't see any threat of temperatures getting below freezing," Taylor said.
